races.name: Weatherbys Global Stallions App Handicap

runners_data.name: Divine Libra
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 196 days with strong jockey booking but faces sprint course challenge from rear

runners_data.name: Double Rush
runners_data.note: Progressive hold-up type returning after long break with two previous course wins but needs to overcome 221-day absence
runners_data.comment: Mostly progressive for Charles Hills; won at this meeting last year; highly respected
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive sort for Charles Hills until disappointing in September on last appearance; commenced last season with two wins, including over C&D at this meeting, and warrants plenty of respect back here on debut for Andrew Balding with a resumption of improvement possible.

runners_data.name: Humam
runners_data.note: Prominent runner switching yards after gelding operation, suited by return to 6f but question marks over stable form
runners_data.comment: Gelded since last run; gives impression he may ideally need a return to 7f
runners_data.spotlight: Gained his final win for previous yard and sole placed effort for current stable over 7f; beaten favourite in Italian Listed race over 6f when last seen; gelded since; may ideally need a step back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Eye Of Dubai
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who excels in autumn conditions making spring reappearance, market will reveal intent
runners_data.comment: By no means certain to shine, having shown best handicap form in autumn months
runners_data.spotlight: Capable of being involved but is by no means certain to shine in this spring reappearance, having shown his best handicap form in autumn months; the market signals may offer further guidance.

runners_data.name: Andesite
runners_data.comment: Record of 0-8 since debut win; first-time headgear needs to help
runners_data.spotlight: Finished last in final start for Karl Burke and midfield effort on reappearance (AW) took his record since debut success to 0-8; chance largely depends on how well he responds to first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Invictus Gold
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up finisher carrying top weight but has solid course record including win here
runners_data.comment: Two attempts over C&D comprise a good third to Double Rush then a ready success; solid
runners_data.spotlight: Ran respectably in AW Listed event when last seen; two attempts over C&D comprise a good third to Double Rush at this meeting 12 months ago and a ready success on 2,000 Guineas day (good); solid chance.

runners_data.name: Dark Thirty
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won this race in 2024 off higher mark, fading tendency but proven course specialist
runners_data.comment: Landed this race off 4lb higher in 2024; second outing for new stable
runners_data.spotlight: Had two attempts at this race when with Richard Hannon, winning off 4lb higher in 2024 and losing his chance with a poor start last year; likely player if back to best in this second outing for new stable.

runners_data.name: Realign
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front-runner returning after 158 days, critical to pace dynamics and holds strong hand

runners_data.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose form tailed off badly with two recent zeros, major question marks despite previous ability
runners_data.comment: Great spell of form has come to an end with duck eggs on last two outings
runners_data.spotlight: Won last year's Portland during a great spell of form that has come to an end with duck eggs in last two appearances; perhaps best watched until she shows clear signs of a revival.

runners_data.name: Coul Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong AW form but limited turf evidence, needs to transfer surface form
runners_data.comment: Won over C&D in last turf attempt; useful AW handicapper since; possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: Successful over C&D (off 15lb lower) seven months ago in last turf attempt and has subsequently developed into a useful AW handicapper; possibilities, provided he transfers the improvement back to this sphere.

runners_data.name: Rousing Encore
runners_data.note: Hold-up finisher who needs further improvement to win at this level despite recent placing
runners_data.comment: Ran creditably on reappearance but this is a step back up in class
runners_data.spotlight: Creditable second at Newcastle (6f, AW) on seasonal debut but looks no certainty to go one better in this stronger grade, especially having gained both wins last year off a 6lb lower mark.

runners_data.name: Diligently
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after long break but has strong course record and excels in spring conditions
runners_data.comment: Both wins in August but ran well on spring reappearance last term
runners_data.spotlight: Has gained both wins during the month of August but ran well (off current mark) on spring reappearance last term and when second to Eternal Sunshine on final outing; gelded since; each-way possibilities.

runners_data.name: Zoulu Chief
runners_data.note: Prominent runner lacking a win over 6f despite consistent placings, trainer out of form

runners_data.name: Baldomero
runners_data.note: Veteran prominent runner with AW form but struggled on turf return, age and surface concerns
runners_data.comment: Second in this race two years ago; comfortably held back on turf 17 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins during his latest spell on AW; close second to Dark Thirty in this contest two years ago but needs to rebound, having been comfortably held returned to turf 17 days ago.

races.paceDynamic: Realign is the only confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms from the gates, setting a sustainable tempo without pressure from other early leaders. The prominent runners Humam, Eye Of Dubai, Dark Thirty, Eternal Sunshine, Diligently, Zoulu Chief and Baldomero will track behind in a mid-pack cluster, while the hold-up merchants Divine Libra, Double Rush, Andestate, Invictus Gold, Coul Angel and Rousing Encore will be anchored at the back. With just one pacemaker over this sprint distance on good ground, the tempo will be steady early before quickening late. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and kick, as they'll have ideal positioning when the pace lifts in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Victory
scenarios.trigger: If Realign sets steady fractions and the prominent pack positions perfectly
scenarios.body: The mid-division horses get first run on the leader while the hold-up horses are caught too far back on the sprint course. Eye Of Dubai, Humam or Eternal Sunshine benefit from tracking the lone leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Realign goes too fast early or the pace collapses completely
scenarios.body: The backmarkers get maximum cover and can unleash late kicks when others tire. Divine Libra and Double Rush benefit from strong finishing speed and quality connections.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire Job
scenarios.trigger: If Realign gets easy fractions and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The Haggas-trained leader exploits the lack of early pace pressure and proves too strong late. Realign holds off all challengers with tactical speed from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If no horse commits to pressuring Realign and they crawl early
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint finish where any style can win from the slow tempo. Dark Thirty and Baldomero benefit from experience in similar tactical battles.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Realign breaks slowly or gets pressured early as the entire pace scenario collapses without the main front-runner
Monitor Dark Thirty for early positioning as his fading tendency could be crucial if tracking the leader too closely
Eye Of Dubai's market moves will signal connections' confidence in his spring reappearance after autumn speciality
Eternal Sunshine needs to show early enthusiasm after two zeros or she becomes a non-runner in the finish
Watch Double Rush's early positioning as his hold-up style needs perfect timing on the sprint course after long absence

races.name: Betway Feilden Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Wareeth
runners_data.note: Front-running style perfectly suited to Newmarket but faces pressure from two other confirmed leaders which could compromise his tactics

runners_data.name: Morshdi
runners_data.note: Natural leader returning from a long 186-day break which raises serious fitness concerns despite his obvious ability
runners_data.comment: Twice-raced colt who is likely to build on his York win and improve further; possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: Twice-raced colt who is brother to a Group 2 winner for his owner and seems likely to improve further; second at Sandown (7f) and went one better at York (1m, good) where he held on by a neck from a rival who subsequently ran well in Group 3; possibilities.

runners_data.name: Poseidon's Warrior
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from powerful Appleby yard who showed excellent stamina when winning over course and distance at Goodwood
runners_data.comment: Drew clear for 5l win at Goodwood and looks a useful prospect for his powerful stable
runners_data.spotlight: Sea The Stars colt who cost 900,000euros as a yearling; close second at Haydock (1m) and justified favouritism from the front at Goodwood (1m1f, good) where he drew clear to win by 5l; represents the powerful Appleby/Buick team and looks a useful prospect; respected.

runners_data.name: Shayem
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with proven Listed class but carries a 3lb penalty and hasn't been seen for 60 days since Saudi Arabia failure
runners_data.comment: Record of 3-4 on home soil features a Listed win; this is a deeper race for the grade
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten long way in Saudi Arabia in sole outing this year; 3-4 on home soil and made all for a clearcut success in Listed event at Pontefract (1m, soft) the final time; probably needs to resume that progress to defy a 3lb penalty in this rather deeper race for the grade.

runners_data.name: Isaac Newton
runners_data.note: Patient style ideally suited to strong pace scenario but Ballydoyle runners can be unpredictable on seasonal returns after 171 days
runners_data.comment: Ballydoyle colt; ran well in the Criterium de Saint-Cloud; leading player on the figures
runners_data.spotlight: Ballydoyle colt who gained his maiden win at Glorious Goodwood then had a couple of French assignments, finishing fifth in a valuable conditions race at Longchamp (form has substance) and good fourth in the Criterium de Saint-Cloud (1m2f Group 1); leading player on the figures.

runners_data.name: Bourbon Blues
runners_data.note: Experienced campaigner with prominent style but already has nine career starts which suggests limited scope for further improvement
runners_data.comment: Useful sort but has raced nine times already and isn't sure to progress much further
runners_data.spotlight: Ended last season at the top of his game, going very close in a 1m2f nursery at Newmarket and a 1m1f Group 3 at Chantilly; has raced nine times already, however, and isn't sure to progress much further this term.

runners_data.name: Command The Stars
runners_data.note: Front-runner who failed to stay 1m2f last time but drops back to a more suitable trip with natural early pace
runners_data.comment: Record of 3-6 features a French Listed win; this looks a stiffer task under 3lb penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 3-6 last term featured a Listed win (1m) on French soil, which followed a good effort in nursery at the York Ebor festival; failed to get home over 1m2f at Saint-Cloud final start; this looks a stiff task under 3lb penalty returned to domestic duty.

races.paceDynamic: Wareeth, Command The Stars and Morshdi will ensure a genuine gallop from the outset, with three confirmed front-runners guaranteed to create a strong tempo over this stamina-testing trip. The pace will be relentless early, likely stringing out the field and setting up a searching examination of stamina reserves in the final three furlongs. This aggressive early gallop will inevitably favour the hold-up horses who can conserve energy early and produce their best work when the pace-setters begin to tire. The tactical advantage lies clearly with Shayem and Isaac Newton, whose patient styles are perfectly suited to exploit the anticipated pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners go too fast early and tie up badly
scenarios.body: The relentless gallop will crack Wareeth, Command The Stars and Morshdi simultaneously, allowing the hold-up horses to sweep past with devastating late runs. Shayem and Isaac Newton possess the tactical pace and stamina reserves to capitalize when the leaders falter.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Dominant Front Runner
scenarios.trigger: If Wareeth or Poseidon's Warrior can control the tempo and kick clear
scenarios.body: One of the pace-setters will dictate terms more cleverly than expected, building a decisive advantage while their rivals battle behind. The winner breaks clear in the final furlong while the hold-up horses are left with too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Bourbon Blues gets the perfect stalking position behind the leaders
scenarios.body: The experienced campaigner will track the pace perfectly and produce a well-timed challenge when the front-runners begin to weaken. His superior racecourse experience and tactical speed will prove decisive in a closely-fought finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes messy with the leaders going too slowly early
scenarios.body: The front-runners will sprint from the three-furlong pole, turning it into an all-out dash that suits horses with natural pace. Command The Stars and Morshdi will benefit from their tactical speed in a race that becomes more about instant acceleration than stamina.

watchPoints.text: Morshdi's fitness after 186 days off could see him fade dramatically if he tries to match the early pace
Watch for Shayem to be caught flat-footed if the pace becomes slow early given his hold-up style
Poseidon's Warrior could find himself trapped behind horses if the three leaders go too fast and bunch up
Isaac Newton's position turning for home will be crucial as he needs the leaders to come back to him
Command The Stars may need to be ridden more patiently than usual if the early pace becomes suicidal

races.name: Betway Earl Of Sefton Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Skukuza
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who needs Ryan Moore to find a clear run in the straight, with 17 days since last run keeping him fresh for this Group 3 assignment.
runners_data.comment: Bit unlucky in 1m1f Group 3 in August; fine efforts in Gr2s latterly; fit and can go well
runners_data.spotlight: Won a valuable Curragh handicap last May and impressed in a Listed win there (also 1m, good) the following month; again had Ryan Moore riding when he looked a shade unlucky in York Group 3 (1m1f, good to firm) in August; finished last year with good efforts in Group 2s at Leopardstown and Longchamp; back in that sort of form when close fifth in Saint-Cloud Group 3 (1m, soft) 17 days ago and he's a likely player with Moore retaking the reins.

runners_data.name: King's Gambit
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up horse returning from a 207-day break under Jamie Spencer, though his recent Listed/Group form has been consistent without winning.
runners_data.comment: 0-9 in Group/Listeds since notable handicap win in 2024; trip on the short side for return
runners_data.spotlight: No wins in nine Group/Listed races since landing the London Gold Cup at Newbury on his seasonal/handicap debut in 2024; frequently ran well, though, albeit with this trip looking a bare minimum when fifth of eight in York Group 3 in August on his penultimate start; can't be confidently ruled out but will need to resume in top order to make his Group-race breakthrough.

runners_data.name: Boiling Point
runners_data.note: Versatile hold-up performer who can lead if needed and boasts excellent Newmarket form, including a Cambridgeshire victory over course and distance.
runners_data.comment: Won Cambridgeshire (C&D) last year; solid comeback in February and bold bid looks likely
runners_data.spotlight: Can lead and goes well here, as he showed again when defying top-weight in the Cambridgeshire handicap over C&D (good to firm) in September; left the impression the run was just needed and/or the trip stretched him when close fourth of five in Winter Derby at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) in February; a bold bid is very much on the cards.

runners_data.name: Prague
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who hasn't won since his Group 2 breakthrough here but has undergone wind surgery and faces a significant 168-day absence.
runners_data.comment: Won Group 2 here in 2024 but has become tricky to place; bottom rated on RPRs
runners_data.spotlight: Announced himself when winning Group 2 here (1m, soft) in September 2024 but 0-8 since and he's become a little tricky to place; had wind surgery in December, which might help, but he's at the bottom of the list on RPRs.

runners_data.name: Persica
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist and defending champion who needs Oisin Murphy to secure a smooth passage, returning from 152 days off the track.
runners_data.comment: Won this last year; big effort to land similar event in June; gelded and needs respect
runners_data.spotlight: Had Ryan Moore on board when winning this race (good to soft) last year and produced another big effort for that rider when landing similar event at Epsom (good) in June; didn't match that form subsequently but has been gelded and no surprise if he goes well in the bid to retain his crown under Oisin Murphy this time; entered in Group 1 Lockinge Stakes.

runners_data.name: Damysus
runners_data.note: The lone prominent runner who will control the tempo under James Doyle, coming back from 186 days off but showing excellent recent form when fresh.
runners_data.comment: Banished memories of Derby flop with Listed and C&D Group 3 wins; key player on return
runners_data.spotlight: Third in good-ground Sandown Classic Trial and second in Group 2 Dante at York (good to firm) last spring; finished last in the Derby but firmly back on track when landing a 1m2f Listed race at Deauville (good to soft) in August and signed off with Group 3 C&D win in October; carries 3lb penalty but holds a Group 1 Lockinge Stakes entry and he's the sort to kick on again this year.

races.paceDynamic: Damysus is the sole confirmed front-runner and will set a sustainable pace without early pressure from this small field of hold-up specialists. The prominent runner will dictate terms through measured fractions, likely quickening approaching the two-furlong pole. With Skukuza, King's Gambit, Boiling Point, Prague and Persica all requiring cover and room to manoeuvre, the race will develop into a tactical affair with horses fanning wide in the straight. This pace scenario strongly favours Damysus and any horse that can track him closely, as the hold-up brigade may struggle to make up ground against controlled fractions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Damysus Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Damysus maintains his prominent position and James Doyle dictates sensible fractions unchallenged.
scenarios.body: The Gosden-trained four-year-old can quicken off his own pace and prove difficult to peg back with tactical advantage. Hold-up horses face the challenge of making ground against a horse who has stolen a march tactically.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and the field bunches entering the final three furlongs.
scenarios.body: Skukuza and Persica can utilise their superior closing kicks with Ryan Moore and Oisin Murphy timing their runs perfectly. The tactical pace will suit their hold-up style as they sweep past a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Boiling Point Tracks Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Boiling Point breaks from his usual hold-up tactics to sit closer to Damysus.
scenarios.body: Burke's charge can use his versatility to race prominently and kick when Damysus comes under pressure. His course form and ability to lead gives him tactical options others lack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Damysus goes too slowly early and the field remains in a tight pack turning for home.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where any horse can win depending on traffic and luck in running. King's Gambit's recent return to form could see Jamie Spencer threading through gaps for an upset.

watchPoints.text: Damysus could steal the race if he gets uncontested fractions and kicks clear before the hold-up horses can respond.
Traffic problems likely in the straight with five hold-up horses needing room simultaneously as they fan wide behind Damysus.
King's Gambit and Prague both return from lengthy breaks exceeding 160 days, making their fitness levels questionable despite decent recent work.
Jockey bookings favour the hold-up horses with Ryan Moore on Skukuza and Oisin Murphy on defending champion Persica.
Boiling Point's versatility could prove crucial if he breaks from his usual hold-up pattern to track Damysus more closely.

races.name: Lanwades Stud Nell Gwyn Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies)

runners_data.name: America Queen
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong course form and 200-day break could be a positive with this demanding pace scenario

runners_data.name: Asmeralda
runners_data.note: Unraced on turf but Gosden yard excels with these types, hold-up style suits the pace dynamic perfectly
runners_data.comment: Successful in Kempton AW event; stable has good record in this race; promising
runners_data.spotlight: Night Of Thunder filly who cost 640,000euros as a yearling; beat a reasonably solid yardstick by half a length, pair clear, in 7f AW event at Kempton four months ago; stable has landed this prize six times, most recently last year; promising contender.

runners_data.name: Silenciosa
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner from Tom Clover needs significant pace collapse to feature prominently in this grade

runners_data.name: Fitzella
runners_data.note: Front-runner with solid Group form but may struggle to dominate against four other confirmed pace-setters
runners_data.comment: Useful filly (Group winner) but may not be crying out for this step back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Group form last summer comprised a success over 6f at Ascot flanked by good efforts at Royal Ascot and Deauville (7f); took a good hold and weakened in the Cheveley Park Stakes, suggesting she may not be crying out for this step back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Mubasimah
runners_data.note: Course winner who showed rallying qualities last time, best placed of the leaders to survive the early battle
runners_data.comment: Won maiden prior to rallying second in the Oh So Sharp, both over C&D; likely player
runners_data.spotlight: Frankel filly who posted a couple of sound front-running performances over C&D last autumn, winning a maiden event (good to firm) and a rallying second in the Oh So Sharp Stakes (Group 3; good ground); open to further improvement and has clear possibilities, especially if again able to dominate.

runners_data.name: Inis Mor
runners_data.note: Progressive front-runner but David Menuisier's poor recent form is concerning despite horse's ability
runners_data.comment: Scored twice on the July course then ran well in Longchamp contest; form has substance
runners_data.spotlight: Thrice-raced filly whose progressive form has plenty of substance; registered novice wins on the Newmarket July course (7f) prior to second of 16 in valuable conditions race at Longchamp (1m) on Arc weekend; may well rate higher still; very solid claims.

runners_data.name: Act Of Kindness
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for in-form Appleby stable, tactical pace gives her options to adapt mid-race

runners_data.name: Awaken
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with Group-level form, George Boughey runner perfectly placed to exploit the strong pace
runners_data.comment: Second in the Albany at Royal Ascot and fourth in the C&D Rockfel; could go well
runners_data.spotlight: Below par in sole start on softer than good; 2yo form otherwise featured a 6f maiden win and two good efforts at Group level, namely second in the Albany at Royal Ascot and fourth in the Rockfel over C&D; could go well.

runners_data.name: Beautify
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner with hold-up style, Ryan Moore booking significant and O'Brien's 3yo fillies are dangerous fresh

runners_data.name: Golden Palace
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who may struggle to make up the ground despite having shown good course form previously
runners_data.comment: Balance of form suggests this is a difficult assignment; upped in distance
runners_data.spotlight: Not disgraced in Listed event at Newmarket (6f) on final 2yo start but remains possibly flattered by the figure she appeared to record here when sixth in the Cheveley Park Stakes and, on balance, faces a difficult task in this field.

runners_data.name: Azleet
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who needs everything to fall right, strong pace should help but lacks the class of main rivals
runners_data.comment: Broadly progressive over 6f but ideally needs to settle better upped in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Broadly progressive 6f form last season culminated in her second in Listed contest at Newmarket (good) when doing well considering she took a good hold and had to wait for a run; ideally needs to settle better upped in distance and this is a harder task.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Breeze
runners_data.note: Front-runner with modest form, likely to be outpaced early by the stronger pace-setters in this field
runners_data.comment: Close second in C&D novice when last seen but this is a much stiffer task
runners_data.spotlight: Kept to the Newmarket tracks last year and steadily got the hang of things, belying 50-1 odds with close second in C&D novice the final time; faces a much stiffer task upped in class and is the only maiden in this field.

runners_data.name: Cherry Baker
runners_data.note: Weakest of the front-runners on ratings, AW winner faces significant step up in class and competition
runners_data.comment: Won well at Southwell but looks highly unlikely to follow up at this level
runners_data.spotlight: Won well at Southwell (6f, AW) to open her account at the fifth attempt but looks highly unlikely to follow up, being towards the bottom of this pack on bare figures and a filly who has no obvious Group potential.

races.paceDynamic: Fitzella, Mubasimah and Inis Mor will ensure a strong early gallop with Harlequin Breeze and Cherry Baker likely to join them, creating a competitive pace battle from the start. The presence of five confirmed front-runners in a 13-runner field guarantees genuine pace throughout the 7f trip. This sustained gallop will set up the race for the hold-up horses like America Queen, Beautify and Awaken who can exploit the inevitable weakening of the pace-setters. The strong pace dynamic heavily favours closers and hold-up performers who can time their challenges late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners engage in a pace duel through the early stages
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will take its toll on the leaders, allowing the class hold-up horses to sweep past in the final furlong. America Queen and Beautify have the highest ratings and proven ability to quicken from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters can dictate without excessive pressure from the others
scenarios.body: A tactical front-runner could steal a march if the others cancel each other out, with Mubasimah's course form making her the most likely beneficiary. Her previous course wins show she can handle the track's demands when getting an easier lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Pack Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady early before quickening significantly from halfway
scenarios.body: Prominent runners can capitalize on a more even tempo by positioning themselves perfectly for a sustained challenge. Act Of Kindness from the Appleby yard has the tactical speed to adapt to different pace scenarios.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Meltdown
scenarios.trigger: If all five front-runners go too fast and stop dramatically in the final quarter-mile
scenarios.body: The entire complexion changes with even unfancied hold-up horses coming into contention from impossible positions. This would create chaos and allow longer-priced closers to emerge from the pack late.

watchPoints.text: Mubasimah and Fitzella could engage in a destructive early battle that compromises both their winning chances
America Queen's 200-day absence combined with her hold-up style creates risk if she needs the run despite the pace setup
Act Of Kindness represents Charlie Appleby who has excellent strike-rate, watch for confident market support
Inis Mor represents David Menuisier whose yard is 0/4 in last 14 days, trainer form could impact performance
Watch the early fractions closely as five confirmed front-runners rarely all commit, someone may take a pull

races.name: Scorthy Champ Standing At Barton British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners_data.name: Beauty Box
runners_data.comment: 95,000gns Space Blues yearling; late April foal; market check required for respected yard
runners_data.spotlight: 95,000gns yearling by Space Blues; second (late April) foal; half-sister to 6f 2yo winner Peel Park (RPR 81); dam 1m3f AW winner (89), half-sister to 6f 2yo Listed winner Straight Answer, out of Group-placed 7f 2yo winning half-sister to 1m2f Group 1 winner Announce; respected yard and market check required on this introduction.

runners_data.name: Call Me Tomorrow
runners_data.comment: 60,000gns yearling by Minzaal; April foal; yard won 2 of the last 4 renewals; likely type
runners_data.spotlight: 60,000gns yearling by Minzaal; third (April) foal; dam 5.7f/6f winner (RPR 89), half-sister to smart 1m-1m6f winner Micro Manage and Listed winners Magnanimous (1m), Thornbrook (1m) and Seisai (7.4f 2yo), out of close relative of 1m4f Group 1 winner Mont Ormel; stable has won two of the last four editions of this and also bagged the Brocklesby last month; a likely type on her first go.

runners_data.name: Havana Lightning
runners_data.comment: 110,000gns Havana Grey (February) foal; interesting pedigree; firm interest with Buick up
runners_data.spotlight: By Havana Grey; 110,000gns foal; second (February) foal; dam 5f AW winner (RPR 68), sister to triple 6f Group 1 winner The Tin Man, half-sister to 6f Group 2 winner Deacon Blues, out of 6f/7f winning sister to useful 6f-1m winner Heretic; that's an interesting pedigree and William Buick is handed the reins for this introduction.

runners_data.name: Jazz Queen
runners_data.comment: 210,000euros Too Darn Hot yearling; April foal; speedy pedigree and yard won this in 2024
runners_data.spotlight: 210,000euros yearling by Too Darn Hot; first (early April) foal; dam placed 5f/6f (RPR 70), sister to winners Flying Sparkle (5f 2yo/7f) and Pres Rapide (5f 2yo), half-sister to winners Winter Power (5f Group 1 Nunthorpe) and Hay Chewed (5f Listed), out of 6f 2yo winner; speedy pedigree and she was the most expensive of these at auction; has to be respected for a yard that won this in 2024 and also introduced a winning juvenile here yesterday.

runners_data.name: Lady Jemima
runners_data.comment: By St Mark's Basilica; April foal; mixed messages on pedigree but will need a market check
runners_data.spotlight: By St Mark's Basilica; third (early April) foal; dam 6f 2yo winner (including Group 1 Prix Morny; RPR 115), half-sister to Listed-placed 1m4f winner Climate Friendly, out of unraced half-sister to US 1m1f Grade 3 winner Gender Agenda, family of Oaks/St Leger winner User Friendly; slightly mixed messages on pedigree for this debut test but will need a market check.

runners_data.name: Magic Effort
runners_data.comment: First runner for sire Good Effort; late March foal; dam 5f 2yo winner
runners_data.spotlight: Fifth (late March) foal; half-sister to 5f AW 2yo winner Share The Profits (RPR 66); dam 5f 2yo winner (100), half-sister to 5f winner Jonboy, is granddaughter of half-sister to 1m Group 2 winner Inchmurrin (dam of high-class 7f performer Inchinor); first runner for sire Good Effort, who won three Listed races for these connections.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Sardinia
runners_data.comment: By Caturra; early March foal; might be best watched unless market suggests otherwise
runners_data.spotlight: By Caturra; seventh (early March) foal; half-sister to four winners including Reward Smile (6f/7f including 2yo/HK/NZ; RPR 92), Demetrius (6f 2yo; 75) and Aish (5f; 67); dam placed 5f/6f (including 2yo; 68), out of half-sister to Group 1 sprint winners Airwave and Jwala; yard was 1-9 in 2yo races last year.

races.name: Molson Coors British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Darzah
runners_data.note: Dubawi newcomer from powerful Haggas/Marquand combination with elite pedigree, but debut runners face tactical disadvantage in moderate pace scenario
runners_data.comment: 375,000gns yearling; by Dubawi out of an AW Listed winner; heed the market signals
runners_data.spotlight: 375,000gns yearling; by Dubawi and first foal of 7f/9.5f winner (including AW Listed; RPR 109); major yard; one of three newcomers in the field; heed the market signals

runners_data.name: Lady Fizz
runners_data.note: Expert Eye filly wearing hood on debut for struggling Donovan yard, best watched rather than backed without market support
runners_data.comment: Expert Eye filly; dam AW scorer; wears hood on debut; best watched
runners_data.spotlight: Expert Eye filly; dam 1m2f AW scorer (RPR 70), out of French 6.5f winning half-sister to Dubai World Cup winner Monterosso; wears hood on debut; best watched.

runners_data.name: Star Of Hope
runners_data.note: Appleby newcomer with Buick aboard represents the most dangerous debut threat given connections' strike rate and tactical awareness

runners_data.name: So Regal
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose Chelmsford third shows clear form, benefits from Ryan Moore booking and Gosden stable's patient approach with fillies
runners_data.comment: Close third, clear of remainder; at Chelmsford; looks sure to progress; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Siblings include a 1m Listed scorer for her connections; beaten favourite but showed promise with close third, clear of remainder, at Chelmsford (7f, AW) in the autumn; looks sure to progress this term; respected.

runners_data.name: Summer In Paris
runners_data.note: Likely pace-setter returning from 169-day break with tongue-tie added, needs to capitalize on uncontested lead to justify front-running tactics
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Newmarket prior to lesser effort on AW; may show progress returned to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Wootton Bassett filly whose autumn efforts comprised a promising fourth at Newmarket (7f) then lesser effort on AW; may show progress returned to turf with tongue-tie fitted.

runners_data.name: Capichera
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner whose close Chelmsford second indicates progress, Walker stable in good form and trip should suit
runners_data.comment: Finished fourth at Newmarket then kept on for close second at Chelmsford; possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: Twice-raced filly who may take another step forward; finished well for fourth over 7f at Newmarket in November then kept on for close second over 1m at Chelmsford (AW); possibilities.

runners_data.name: Silver Lake
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who found 7f too sharp previously, expensive yearling whose pedigree suggests this longer trip will help significantly
runners_data.comment: Seemed to find 7f too sharp at Newmarket in sole 2yo start; open to improvement
runners_data.spotlight: 420,000gns yearling; seemed to find 7f too sharp, in keeping with pedigree, at Newmarket (behind Capichera) in sole 2yo start; open to improvement over this longer distance.

runners_data.name: Lyrics Of Life
runners_data.note: Pure hold-up horse with best RPR rating but style disadvantage in likely moderate pace, needs strong tempo to unleash finishing kick

races.paceDynamic: Summer In Paris will likely set the early pace unopposed, with So Regal and Capichera tracking prominently but neither horse aggressive enough to create serious early pressure. This setup creates a moderate tempo that builds gradually, allowing the proven runners to stay in touch while potentially exposing the three newcomers (Darzah, Lady Fizz, Star Of Hope) who lack racecourse experience. The sustainable gallop and lack of early burn-up strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed who can position close to the pace rather than pure hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Proven Form Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the three newcomers fail to fire on debut...
scenarios.body: The race becomes a battle between the four experienced fillies, with the moderate pace suiting those who showed form last year. So Regal's promising Chelmsford third and Capichera's consistent efforts make them best equipped to capitalize.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Godolphin Newcomer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Star Of Hope brings elite debut form to match her connections...
scenarios.body: Charlie Appleby's newcomer uses William Buick's positioning skills to track the pace and strike decisively, benefiting from both the tactical setup and superior raw ability. The lack of early pressure allows her to travel smoothly into contention.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Summer In Paris sets too steady a tempo early...
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop becomes pedestrian, allowing Lyrics Of Life and Silver Lake to make their ground from the back despite their hold-up styles. The lack of true pace exposure benefits those with finishing kicks over pure speed horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Summer In Paris maintains her advantage throughout...
scenarios.body: The early leader capitalizes on soft fractions and her 169-day break to sustain her effort, with the tongue-tie potentially helping her breathing. The prominent runners fail to mount sufficient challenge in the straight.

watchPoints.text: Watch for any market moves on the three newcomers, particularly Darzah and Star Of Hope, as connections may know significantly more than form suggests
Monitor if Summer In Paris gets an easy lead early - if unchallenged through the first half-mile, she becomes very dangerous despite long absence
Silver Lake's response to the step up in trip is crucial given her expensive purchase price and pedigree suggesting mile will suit better
So Regal's market position relative to the newcomers will indicate connections' confidence after her promising debut effort
Any pace pressure on Summer In Paris early could set up the race perfectly for Lyrics Of Life's finishing kick despite her hold-up disadvantage

races.name: Betway Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: High Storm
runners_data.note: Prominent racer improving this season with competitive handicap mark, strong recent form suggests he can handle this company
runners_data.comment: Won 1m2f Doncaster maiden; competitive mark for handicap debut and he'll be staying on
runners_data.spotlight: Markedly better this season when second at Southwell (1m3f, AW) and winning from the front in a maiden at Doncaster (1m2f, good to soft); has a competitive mark for this handicap debut and he'll be staying on.

runners_data.name: Oratorical
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning after 155 days off but showed substantial improvement when winning at Nottingham, William Buick a positive
runners_data.comment: Won novice at Nottingham (1m, heavy) in October and it looks like he'll surely stay
runners_data.spotlight: Three months off before showing substantial improvement to win 12-runner novice at Nottingham (1m, heavy) in October; creditable sixth of seven in French Listed race on final outing; better is needed on this handicap/seasonal debut but it looks like he'll surely stay.

runners_data.name: Ranga Tang
runners_data.note: Prominent type who showed ability on good ground at Newmarket, the 158-day break and headgear change adds intrigue
runners_data.comment: Neck second in AW novice (8.6f; made most) in November; will stay; cheekpieces go on
runners_data.spotlight: Showed ability on good ground at Newmarket (1m) and Goodwood (1m1f) before his neck second of ten in a novice at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW; made most) in November; will stay 1m2f+; cheekpieces go on and he has what looks a competitive mark for handicap/seasonal debut.

runners_data.name: Tailgunner Joe
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid Meydan form over similar distances, proven stamina for this trip makes him dangerous late
runners_data.comment: Has been running at Meydan; needs to find extra but there are no doubts over his fitness
runners_data.spotlight: Fair form on varied turf as 2yo; rather better in his seven-race campaign at Meydan in December-March, including a 1m win and he shaped as if he stayed 1m1f on latest start; needs to find extra but, unlike most of these, there are no doubts over his fitness.

runners_data.name: Waterford Castle
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who has been running consistently this year, Tom Marquand booking suggests stable confidence despite moderate odds
runners_data.comment: Odds-on defeats on AW (7f/8.6f) this year were his best form but he needs to find extra
runners_data.spotlight: Showed promise in three turf runs for Ralph Beckett last summer; turned over at 4-6 this year at Wolverhampton (AW) in a 7f maiden and 8.6f handicap, which were his best form and he's shaping as if worth a go at 1m2f but he needs to find extra.

runners_data.name: Evanesco
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 193 days but won impressively in heavy ground at Salisbury, needs to prove fitness
runners_data.comment: 2nd at Goodwood (7f) and win at Salisbury (1m, heavy) were easily best of five 2yo races
runners_data.spotlight: Close second in a Goodwood maiden (7f, good to soft) and dominant novice win at Salisbury (1m, heavy) were easily best of his five efforts as 2yo; two of the others were in France; needs to resume progress but will stay 1m2f and is one to consider.

runners_data.name: The Joker
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who needs to settle better after making running unsuccessfully, 166-day break could help his temperament
runners_data.comment: Could do with settling a little better on this handicap/seasonal debut but bred to stay
runners_data.spotlight: Minor honours in his three starts on varied ground last summer, before a modest show in 7f novice here in October; could do with settling a little better (made most penultimate start; raced very prominently on latest) on this handicap/seasonal debut but he is bred to stay 1m2f.

runners_data.name: Archers Bay
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner switching from blinkers to cheekpieces, likely to face more pressure than ideal in this field
runners_data.comment: Ex-Aidan O'Brien; made all in novice at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) in December; needs better
runners_data.spotlight: Some improvement in maidens in the mud for Aidan O'Brien in the autumn; 30,000gns purchase and first-time cheekpieces (replacing blinkers) when getting off the mark at first time of asking for new yard in seven-runner novice at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) in December, making all; needs a chunk of improvement on this handicap debut but the trip should not be a problem.

runners_data.name: Impossible Mission
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose sole turf run was poor but won well on AW debut, big question mark over surface switch
runners_data.comment: 9.4f AW winner in November but ran poorly on last month's reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Sole turf run was debut (on good; last of nine); improved on handicap debut when seeing off his five rivals at Wolverhampton (upped to 9.4f, AW) in November, but ran poorly at Lingfield (1m2f, AW; raced widest and a bit freely) on last month's reappearance; needs to resume improvement.

races.paceDynamic: Archers Bay will attempt to lead from the start but faces immediate pressure from four prominent runners (High Storm, Ranga Tang, Evanesco, The Joker) who all want to race within striking distance. This creates a moderate pace with congestion 2-3 furlongs out as the prominent pack converges while hold-up horses (Oratorical, Tailgunner Joe, Waterford Castle, Impossible Mission) launch their challenges. The early pace pressure on Archers Bay will likely see him falter, setting up the race for horses that can either get good position without leading or finish strongly from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can avoid the early scrimmaging and hold-up horses with proven finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Clash
scenarios.trigger: If High Storm and Evanesco can secure good early position without getting caught in traffic
scenarios.body: The pair can dictate from 3f out while Archers Bay fades and the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground on good going. Their class and tactical speed becomes decisive in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong with prominent runners scrapping for position
scenarios.body: Oratorical and Tailgunner Joe benefit from the setup with their proven finishing kicks getting them home. The pace collapse allows them to sweep past the tired leaders in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Archers Bay Wire Job
scenarios.trigger: If Archers Bay gets an uncontested lead and the prominent runners mark each other
scenarios.body: The leader can dictate fractions and hold off late challenges despite his moderate ability. The hold-up horses have too much to do while the prominent pack neutralizes each other.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is surprisingly steady with Archers Bay unopposed early
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from 2f out where any of the nine can win in a blanket finish. Form and class become secondary to whoever gets the clearest run in the straight.

watchPoints.text: Archers Bay may fold quickly if the prominent runners put him under early pressure, creating a pace collapse scenario
Watch for traffic problems 2-3 furlongs out where High Storm, Evanesco, Ranga Tang and The Joker could all converge simultaneously
Oratorical and Tailgunner Joe need the pace to be genuine early to set up their finishing kicks from the rear
Evanesco returning after 193 days off needs to prove his fitness lasts the final furlong after showing early pace
The moderate early pace could favor Waterford Castle and Impossible Mission if they can get competitive positions turning in
